To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interior permanent magnet (IPM) machines with different rotor structures can achieve high torque density and efficiency.
the interior permanent-magnet machine with the rotor topologies of the spoke type and the hybrid spoke/segment type are the best candidates for the traction applications.
the interior permanent-magnet machine with a rotor topology that includes a double-layer concentrated winding has the best overall characteristics for high-performance traction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of IPM machines with different rotor topologies for traction applications.
the design, analysis and comparison of five IPM machines with different rotor topologies.

the following issues: (1) to investigate the characteristics and performance of five IPM machines, including their torque density, overload capability, and flux-weakening capability; (2) to evaluate the d-axis and q-axis inductances of the five IPM machines; (3) to analyze the back-electromotive forces (EMFs) of the five machines; and (4) to compare the performance of the five machines and give some guidelines for machine selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a rotor topology of IPM machine should be carefully designed according to the specific requirements of a particular application.
the rotor topology with concentrated windings and a rotor with concentrated permanent magnets is the best choice for high-performance traction application.
the interior rotor topology with a concentrated winding has the best overall characteristics, and is the most promising machine type for traction application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rotor with concentrated winding and the rotor with concentrated permanent magnets have better overload capability, the rotor with distributed winding and the rotor without permanent magnets have better flux weakening performance and the rotor with distributed permanent magnets has better torque density.

the rotor topology should not be selected based on the maximum torque density and maximum power density only, but also based on the torque ripple, flux-weakening capability, overload capability, and the d-q axis inductive characteristics.
the IPM machine with a single-layer winding rotor has better performance in overload capability, flux-weakening capability, and torque density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rotor topology has a significant impact on the machine performance and design trade-offs.
the flux-barrier rotor is a good candidate for high torque density applications.
the rotor design is a critical factor in determining the performance of IPM machine for electric vehicle applications.
